text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet told Gennady Seleznyov, visiting Speaker of Russia's Duma, that Vietnam wants to intensify traditional and bilateral cooperation with Russia to develop energy sources, particularly oil and gas.

-- Canada has agreed to grant $2 million for a rural finance project to support the People's Credit Fund network's activities in receiving and relending loans from the on-going rural credit programme assisted by the Asian Development Bank.

-- PetroVietnam General Director Ngo Thuong San said Vietnam's oil and gas industry would remain stable despite continuing difficulties. He said that in the first two months of this year, PetroVietnam exploited 1.2 million tonnes of crude oil and was aiming for a full-year total of 9.6 million tonnes compared with 8.5 million in 1996. He also said that production could peak at 20 million tonnes by 2005.
-- The Vietnam Coffee Corporation (Vinacafe) will spend 80 billion dong ($7.14 million) expanding coffee production in 1997.

-- The United States and Vietnam have begun a programme for exchanging information on international trade and market management policies. The programme will be the main topic of discussion at a five-day seminar which the U.S. Commerce Department and the Vietnam-United States Commerce Council opened in Hanoi on Monday.
-- The World Bank and the Caisse Francaise du Developpement have agreed to provide some $120 million for Vietnam to develop rubber farms in the central highlands.
-- The Vietnam Paper Corporation and South Korea's Daewoo Group are preparing a joint venture contract to build a $60-million plant specialising in cement packaging paper.
-- Vietnam will auction 50 billion dong ($4.46 million) worth of one-year Treasury notes on Wednesday. The targetted annual interest rate for the sale is 11.50 percent.
-- The Asian Development Bank has granted a loan of $32 million for the Vietnam Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development.
-- The Vietnam War Veterans' Association has became a full member of the Veterans' Confederation of Asean Countries.
-- The state oil and gas firm PetroVietnam announced that Vietnam had rejected a proposal by foreign partners and would go it alone in building the country's first oil refinery in Dung Quat.
-- Vietnam is planning to have its own telecommunication satelite by 2000.
